\chapter{Divergences}\label{chap:divergences}

\section*{At a glance}
\begin{itemize}
\item \lead{Source} \code{doc/DIVERGENCES.md}, rendered by \code{blueprint/scripts/render\_registers.py}; the sections below are the register's own text.
\item \lead{Entries} 0.
\end{itemize}

This register lists every place where the verification code, or the statements it proves, diverge from the references of spec \S{}3.1--\S{}3.2 --- Letouzey, "A New Extraction for Coq" (\S{}3.1), and Sozeau et al., "Correct and Complete Type Checking and Certified Erasure for Coq, in Coq" (\S{}3.2), including its MetaRocq sources. The verification effort follows these references as closely as the differences between Lean's kernel/\texttt{lean4lean}'s model and Rocq/PCUIC/MetaRocq allow; every place it does not, for any reason, is recorded here.

Each entry has an id \texttt{DV-\textless{}n\textgreater{}} and exactly these fields:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} file and declaration on the \texttt{verification} branch that carries the divergence.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the paper section/figure/theorem (\S{}3.1 or \S{}3.2) and the MetaRocq \texttt{file:identifier} it corresponds to.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the concrete difference between our artifact and the reference artifact.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the concrete reason the divergence is necessary --- a difference between Lean's kernel and CIC, a gap in what \texttt{lean4lean} \texttt{master} provides, a scope boundary from \S{}2 of the spec, or similar. This field must name a real constraint; "it was simpler" or "we chose to" is not a forcing reason.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} the alternative(s) that would have kept the divergence from existing, and why each was rejected.
\end{itemize}

An entry without a forcing reason is a defect, not a divergence: it must be removed and the statement or definition restated to match the reference instead.

Entries are headed \texttt{\#\#\# DV-\textless{}n\textgreater{}}. They cite declarations by full name in backquotes (ours as \texttt{EraseProof.\textless{}name\textgreater{}}, lean4lean's as \texttt{Lean4Lean.\textless{}name\textgreater{}}), our files by their path in the repository (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}...}), lean4lean \texttt{master} sources by path and line (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}...lean:\textless{}line\textgreater{}}), and MetaRocq sources by path relative to the MetaRocq repository and line. Check C9 of \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}scripts/\allowbreak{}check.sh} fails if a cited \texttt{EraseProof.*} or \texttt{Lean4Lean.*} name is not a declaration, a cited file or line does not exist, an entry's fields differ from the list above, or an entry's artifact field cites no declaration of \texttt{EraseProof}.

The blueprint renders this register.

\section{\texorpdfstring{Entries}{Entries}}\label{reg:entries}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-1}{DV-1}}\label{reg:dv-1}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}: the source semantics evaluates Lean terms (\texttt{Expr}), the eraser's input, whose types are those of their images under \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} in lean4lean's syntax \texttt{VExpr}; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Erases}: the erasure relation relates these Lean terms, under a lean4lean context \texttt{Lean4Lean.VLCtx} of their images, to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} terms.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}; MetaCoq paper \S{}5.6) and the erasure relation \texttt{erases} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}; \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), both on PCUIC terms, the syntax that PCUIC's typing judges; Letouzey \S{}3.1 (CIC terms).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the syntax that evaluates and the syntax that is typed are different: \texttt{Expr}, with \texttt{let} (\texttt{Expr.letE}) and metadata (\texttt{Expr.mdata}), for evaluation, and lean4lean's \texttt{VExpr} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VExpr.lean:7-13}), which has neither, for typing; \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} relates them. In PCUIC both are the same terms. \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} evaluates a \texttt{let} as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta} does (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:241}): the value first, then the body with the value substituted; metadata is transparent (rule \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.mdata}). \texttt{EraseProof.Erases} relates \texttt{Expr} to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} as \texttt{erases} relates PCUIC terms, under a context of \texttt{VExpr} images: its binder rules \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.lam} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.letE} take the translation of the binder's type (and of a \texttt{let} value) as a premise, and extend the context with it, where \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLambda} and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:93}, \texttt{:96}) extend \texttt{\ensuremath{\Gamma}} with the PCUIC binder itself; a \texttt{let} erases to a \texttt{tLetIn} of the erased value, as in \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn}, and metadata is transparent (rule \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.mdata}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser consumes \texttt{Expr}, and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} image of a \texttt{let} evaluates its value first (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:134}; rule \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval.zeta}). \texttt{VExpr} has no \texttt{let}: \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} translates \texttt{let x := v; b} to the translation of \texttt{b} in a context whose entry for \texttt{x} is the translation of \texttt{v} (rule \texttt{EraseProof.TrS.letE}, as rule \texttt{letE} of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:97-101}), that is, with the value substituted. A semantics on \texttt{VExpr} therefore never evaluates a \texttt{let} value, and relating it to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation, which does, when the value diverges would need a normalization theorem, which lean4lean \texttt{master} does not have. The erasure relation that the simulation carries along \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} is on the same syntax, and its context, in which erasability (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasableS}) is judged, is a lean4lean typing context, whose entries are \texttt{VExpr}.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a semantics on \texttt{VExpr}: with the recursive \texttt{unsafe def loop : A \ensuremath{\to} A := fun x =\textgreater{} loop x} and \texttt{a : A}, the term \texttt{let x := loop a; a} has the image \texttt{a}, a value, while its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} image evaluates \texttt{loop a} first and diverges.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-2}{DV-2}}\label{reg:dv-2}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.TrS}, the translation of Lean terms into lean4lean's model.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's translation of Template terms into PCUIC terms, \texttt{trans} (\texttt{template-pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}TemplateToPCUIC.v:63}; the MetaCoq paper's "certified type-preserving translation from Coq's syntax to PCUIC's syntax", \S{}9), which erasure (\S{}7) consumes; the translation \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} follows is lean4lean's \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:75}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} has the rules of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} except \texttt{lit} and \texttt{proj}: literals (\texttt{Expr.lit}) and projections (\texttt{Expr.proj}) have no translation, so terms containing them are outside the fragment. Like \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} and unlike \texttt{trans}, it is a relation (its image is unique: \texttt{EraseProof.TrS.det}). Every derivation of \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} is one of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} (test \texttt{EraseProof.Test.TrS.toTrExprS}, whose statement reaches the \texttt{sorry} of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the lemmas of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} handle \texttt{proj} with \texttt{sorry} proofs (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Lemmas.lean:642,723,727,893,938,1240,1509}); reusing them puts projection sorries into a fragment without projections. The \texttt{lit} rule translates a literal through constructors of \texttt{Nat} and \texttt{String} (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.ContainsLits}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:70}), which are inductive types, absent from the model (DV-6). Secondarily, projections are translated through \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj}, a \texttt{sorry} definition (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:68}), which every hypothesis stated with \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} would mention.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} with a side condition excluding projections and literals: the hypotheses would still mention \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj}, and its lemmas would reach the \texttt{sorry} proofs of the \texttt{proj} cases.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-3}{DV-3}}\label{reg:dv-3}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Env.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}, with \texttt{EraseProof.TrConst}, \texttt{EraseProof.TrDef} and \texttt{EraseProof.findDecl}: the relation between a program's declarations and their model in lean4lean. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Env/\allowbreak{}Unfold.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.SubEnv}: every declaration of a list is the program's declaration of that name. \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} types its term in the model of the program \texttt{P}, and evaluates it (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}) and relates its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps}) over an evaluation environment whose declarations form a sub-environment of \texttt{P} (its hypothesis \texttt{hsub}); and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Restrict.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.restrict}, with \texttt{EraseProof.DepClosed} and \texttt{EraseProof.ConstsIn}: an evaluation over \texttt{P} is an evaluation over every sub-environment that is closed under the dependencies of its members and contains the evaluated term's constants. \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases}, types its term in the model of \texttt{P} and relates the eraser's output with the atoms and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies of the dependency closure \texttt{decls} that \texttt{Erasure.collectDeps} computes, a sub-environment of \texttt{P} (\texttt{EraseProof.collectDeps\_\allowbreak{}sub}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the well-formed global environment \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext \ensuremath{\Sigma}} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}; MetaCoq paper \S{}3.6), a hypothesis of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}), whose declarations are a newest-first list searched by \texttt{lookup\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Environment.v:483}); and lean4lean's relation between a kernel environment and its model, \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Environment/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:128}), which \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} restates. MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} types, evaluates and erases in the one environment \texttt{\ensuremath{\Sigma}}; its \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) evaluates the source term over the whole environment and the erased term over the erasure of the dependency closure \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}global\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1602}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the environment is a newest-first list of Lean \texttt{ConstantInfo}s, searched like \texttt{lookup\_\allowbreak{}env} by \texttt{EraseProof.findDecl}, instead of a Lean \texttt{Environment} or the constant map of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'}. \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} has the rules \texttt{axiom}, \texttt{defn}, \texttt{thm}, \texttt{opaque} and \texttt{mutualDef} (named \texttt{block}) of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} at safety \texttt{.unsafe}, with \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} in place of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS}; \texttt{EraseProof.TrConst} and \texttt{EraseProof.TrDef} restate \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrConstant} and \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrDefVal} without their safety conjunct, which holds for every declaration at \texttt{.unsafe}. It has no \texttt{ignore} rule (at \texttt{.unsafe} no declaration is ignored), no \texttt{quot} rule, no \texttt{induct} rule, and no freshness premise on a constant map (a name is fresh in the model because \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.addConst} succeeds). It has one premise that \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} lacks: the field \texttt{all} is what Lean's elaborator sets, the declaration's own name for a single definition, theorem or opaque constant, and the block's names in order for each member of a block. Every \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} gives a \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} at \texttt{.unsafe} of the same model, with a constant map that holds each of the program's declarations under its name (test \texttt{EraseProof.Test.ProgEnv.toTrEnv'}, whose statement reaches the \texttt{sorry} definitions \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj} and \texttt{Lean4Lean.VInductDecl.WF}). Compared with \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext \ensuremath{\Sigma}}, the environment has no inductive declarations, and its typing is lean4lean's (DV-5). Two environments take the place of \texttt{\ensuremath{\Sigma}} in \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct}: typing is in the model of the whole program \texttt{P}, while evaluation, the atoms and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies are over the evaluation environment, whose declarations are a sub-environment of \texttt{P} (\texttt{EraseProof.SubEnv}), in the eraser's case the dependency closure it computes (\texttt{collectDeps}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Collect.lean}); \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.restrict} moves an evaluation over \texttt{P} to such a closure.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} a Lean \texttt{Environment} always contains the inductive types of \texttt{Init}, and \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} at \texttt{.unsafe} relates no constant map that contains an inductive type (lean4lean's \texttt{TrEnv'.no\_\allowbreak{}inductInfo}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Environment/\allowbreak{}Extension.lean:18}), because lean4lean \texttt{master} has no inductive types (DV-6); so a program is stated as an inductive-free list of declarations. The rule \texttt{quot} needs a constant named \texttt{Eq} (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.QuotReady}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Quot.lean:13}), which is an inductive type in every Lean environment. \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} is stated with \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS}, whose projection rule and lemmas carry \texttt{sorry} (DV-2). The eraser reads \texttt{all} to lay out a block of mutual definitions (\texttt{visitMutual}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), and lean4lean's kernel does not check it (\texttt{addDefinition} to \texttt{addMutual}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Environment.lean:36-118}), so the premise states what the elaborator guarantees. Evaluation and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies range over the closure, not over \texttt{P}, because the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant of a declaration is found by its kername (DV-14), and kernames are injective only on the closure, where \texttt{collectDeps} checks it: two constants of \texttt{P} outside the closure may share a kername (SHIPPING-CHANGES R-3), and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment the eraser emits contains declarations of the closure only.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} of a real Lean environment, which does not hold for any (\texttt{TrEnv'.no\_\allowbreak{}inductInfo}); \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'} of a kernel environment built from the program's declarations, whose hypotheses would mention \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj} through \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS} (DV-2); no \texttt{all} premise, under which the eraser's reading of \texttt{all} is unconstrained; one environment \texttt{P} for typing, evaluation and dependencies, as in \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct}, under which kername injectivity fails for programs with colliding names outside the closure; the computed closure itself as the environment of typing, under which the hypotheses would depend on the eraser's own computation rather than on the program.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-4}{DV-4}}\label{reg:dv-4}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Erasability.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.IsErasable}, with \texttt{EraseProof.IsArity}: a term of the model is erasable when some type of it is an arity, or has a sort whose level is equivalent to zero.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{isErasable} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:18}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), which asks for a type \texttt{T} of the term that is an arity (\texttt{isArity}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:29}) or whose sort \texttt{u} satisfies \texttt{Sort.is\_\allowbreak{}propositional u} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Universes.v:1528}: \texttt{u} is \texttt{Prop} or \texttt{SProp}); Letouzey Def. 1 (type schemes) and the \ensuremath{\Box} clause of Def. 3.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the propositional case asks for \texttt{u \ensuremath{\approx} .zero}, that is, the level \texttt{u} evaluates to zero under every assignment of the level parameters (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VLevel.Equiv}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VLevel.lean:58}, over \texttt{Lean4Lean.VLevel.eval}, \texttt{:34-39}), in place of \texttt{Sort.is\_\allowbreak{}propositional u}, and has no \texttt{SProp} case. \texttt{EraseProof.IsArity} is \texttt{isArity} on \texttt{Lean4Lean.VExpr}: sorts and \ensuremath{\Pi}-types ending in a sort, without the \texttt{tLetIn} clause of \texttt{isArity}.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Lean has no \texttt{SProp}, and its \texttt{Prop} is \texttt{Sort 0}, where a level is an expression over level parameters with \texttt{succ}, \texttt{max} and \texttt{imax} (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VLevel}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VLevel.lean:8-13}). A sort is therefore a proposition under every instantiation of the level parameters exactly when its level evaluates to zero under every assignment: \texttt{Sort (imax u 0)} is \texttt{Prop} for every \texttt{u}, while \texttt{Sort u} is \texttt{Prop} for some instantiations only. lean4lean's typing identifies sorts whose levels are equivalent in this sense (\texttt{sortDF}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:22}), so only a test up to this equivalence is invariant under definitional equality. \texttt{Lean4Lean.VExpr} has no \texttt{let} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VExpr.lean:7-13}): \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} translates a \texttt{let} to its body with the value substituted, so no model type has a \texttt{tLetIn} clause to follow.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} the syntactic test \texttt{u = .zero} (a type whose sort is written \texttt{Sort 0}): it misses propositions whose sort is written \texttt{imax u 0} or \texttt{max 0 0}, which the model equates with \texttt{Sort 0}, so erasability would depend on how a sort is written rather than on its level.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-5}{DV-5}}\label{reg:dv-5}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}: all typing in \texttt{EraseProof} is lean4lean's typing judgment \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.IsDefEq} (through \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.HasType}, \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.IsType}, \texttt{Lean4Lean.VExpr.WF}), as in the premises of \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} and the conclusion of \texttt{EraseProof.TrS.wf}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC typing, MetaCoq paper \S{}3.3 (cumulativity) and \S{}3.5 (typing, Fig. 21), MetaRocq \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:198} \texttt{typing} with \texttt{type\_\allowbreak{}Cumul} (\texttt{:294}), on which erasure (\S{}7) is stated; Letouzey \S{}3.1 (CIC).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the judgment has definitional proof irrelevance (\texttt{proofIrrel}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:51}) and \ensuremath{\eta} for functions (\texttt{eta}, \texttt{:48}; PCUIC has no \ensuremath{\eta}, MetaCoq paper \S{}2.4); it has no cumulativity (conversion only, \texttt{defeqDF}, \texttt{:44}); levels have the operator \texttt{imax} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VLevel.lean:12}), in which the sort of a \ensuremath{\Pi}-type is stated (\texttt{forallEDF}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:40}), and are compared up to evaluation (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VLevel.Equiv}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}VLevel.lean:58}, in \texttt{sortDF}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:22}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser's inputs are Lean terms, typed by Lean's kernel; the spec (\S{}2) requires lean4lean \texttt{master} as the model of that kernel, and it models Lean's theory, not PCUIC.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} none: PCUIC typing does not type Lean terms (it has cumulativity, and neither definitional proof irrelevance nor \texttt{imax}), so no judgment closer to the reference types the eraser's inputs.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-6}{DV-6}}\label{reg:dv-6}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} the fragment: the source terms \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} translates (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}); the programs \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} relates to a model (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Env.lean}); the rules of the source evaluation \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}); and the rules of the erasure relation \texttt{EraseProof.Erases} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's erasure relation \texttt{erases} in full (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), with its rules \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConstruct} (\texttt{:106}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{:109}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tProj} (\texttt{:118}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{:122}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCoFix} (\texttt{:129}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tPrim} (\texttt{:137}), and PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}) with its \ensuremath{\iota}-rules; Letouzey Def. 3 (all cases of \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}, fixpoints) and Def. 8 (\ensuremath{\iota}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} no constructors, case analysis, projections, source fixpoints, cofixpoints, primitive values or evars, and no \ensuremath{\iota}-reduction: \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} has no rule for \texttt{Expr.proj}, \texttt{Expr.lit} or \texttt{Expr.mvar}, and Lean's \texttt{Expr} has no node for constructors, case analysis, fixpoints or cofixpoints (in Lean these are constants of inductive declarations, which \texttt{EraseProof.TrS} translates only as constants of the model's environment). \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} has no rule for inductive or quotient declarations (DV-3), so a program in scope declares axioms, definitions, theorems, opaque constants and blocks of mutual definitions only. \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} has no \ensuremath{\iota}-rule and no rule for projections, fixpoint terms, cofixpoints, constructors or primitive values: its rules are \ensuremath{\beta}, \ensuremath{\zeta}, \ensuremath{\delta}, the two recursion rules of DV-7, the atom rules of DV-11, application congruence, metadata and the values \ensuremath{\lambda}, sort and \ensuremath{\Pi}. \texttt{EraseProof.Erases} has no counterpart of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConstruct}, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase}, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tProj}, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix}, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCoFix} or \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tPrim}: its rules are those of variables, \ensuremath{\lambda}, \texttt{let}, application, constants (with DV-7's \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec}), metadata and \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} lean4lean \texttt{master} has no inductive types: \texttt{Lean4Lean.VInductDecl.WF} and \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.addInduct} are \texttt{sorry} definitions (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Inductive.lean:5,7}), so the model has no constructors, recursors or \ensuremath{\iota}-reduction; projections are translated through the \texttt{sorry} definition \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:68}); literals are values of the inductive types \texttt{Nat} and \texttt{String} (DV-2); the kernel's terms have no metavariables.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} axiomatized inductive types (types, constructors and recursors as constants, \ensuremath{\iota} as definitional equalities) in an ordered environment: the rule \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.Ordered.defeq} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Lemmas.lean:258}) admits any well-typed definitional equality, such as \texttt{Sort 0 \ensuremath{\equiv} (Sort 0 \ensuremath{\to} Sort 0)}, so the injectivity of \ensuremath{\Pi}-types that the simulation proof needs fails there; master proves that injectivity (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.IsDefEqU.forallE\_\allowbreak{}inv}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Injectivity.lean:23}) only under \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.WF}, whose inductive part is the \texttt{sorry} definition above.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-7}{DV-7}}\label{reg:dv-7}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}: \texttt{EraseProof.RecursiveDecl} (with \texttt{EraseProof.OccursV}), the rules \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.fixAtom} and \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.fixApp} of \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}, the value shape \texttt{EraseProof.SrcValue.fixConst} and the head condition \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksCong}: recursion in the source semantics; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}: the rule \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec} of \texttt{EraseProof.Erases} and the admissible targets \texttt{EraseProof.RecIn}: recursion in the erasure relation; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Deps.lean}: \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock}, the recursive branch of \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}, and \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased}: recursion in the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Simulation/\allowbreak{}Fix.lean}: \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}fixAtom} and \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}fixApp}, the cases of the simulation for the two recursion rules. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.RcClosed}: the admissible targets are closed, a hypothesis of the substitution lemmas \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.inst} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.inst\_\allowbreak{}let}; the fixpoints stored in a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment whose bodies are closed (\texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed}) are closed (\texttt{EraseProof.RecIn.rcClosed}, \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Simulation/\allowbreak{}Cases.lean}), which is why \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} has the hypothesis \texttt{hlc}. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Glue.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.isRecursiveDecl\_\allowbreak{}eq}: the pure backend's recursion test \texttt{Erasure.isRecursiveDecl} is \texttt{EraseProof.RecursiveDecl}. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Block.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.visitMutual\_\allowbreak{}rec\_\allowbreak{}step}: \texttt{visitMutual} on a recursive declaration (its test is \texttt{EraseProof.RecursiveDecl}, by \texttt{EraseProof.visitMutual\_\allowbreak{}test} and \texttt{EraseProof.isRecursiveDecl\_\allowbreak{}eq}) erases the whole block and registers member \texttt{j} as \texttt{tFix defs j} of an erased block (\texttt{EraseProof.block\_\allowbreak{}finish}, \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's fixpoints: the term \texttt{tFix}, a value (\texttt{atom}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:51}), unfolded when applied by \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{:273}) and excluded as a head of \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}app\_\allowbreak{}cong} (\texttt{:311}, \texttt{isFixApp}); their erasure \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122}); Letouzey Def. 3 (the fixpoint case of \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}); \texttt{globals\_\allowbreak{}erased\_\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EDeps.v:594}), which gives every declared constant an erased \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration whose body has erased dependencies; and the \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} case of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:579-748}). \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} has no hypothesis on the closedness of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment, and its substitution lemma \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}subst0} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ESubstitution.v:612}) no closedness premise; MetaRocq derives \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}) for an erased environment (\texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}global\_\allowbreak{}closed\_\allowbreak{}env}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:1236}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean has no fixpoint term; recursion lives in constants. A constant is recursive (\texttt{EraseProof.RecursiveDecl}) when its block has several members or its value mentions its own name in a value position (\texttt{EraseProof.OccursV}). \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} treats a recursive constant as a PCUIC \texttt{tFix} with \texttt{rarg = 0}: the constant evaluates to itself (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.fixAtom}, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} to a \texttt{tFix} value), and applied to an argument it evaluates the argument, then its value, at the occurrence's levels, applied to the argument's value (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.fixApp}, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} with \texttt{rarg = 0} and no earlier arguments). Recursive constants of every type are values, including those whose value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}: with \texttt{unsafe def x : A \ensuremath{\to} A := x}, \texttt{x} is a value of \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}, as its image, a \texttt{tFix}, is a value of \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}, while Lean's own evaluation of \texttt{x} (\texttt{lean -{}-run}) does not terminate. Non-recursive constants unfold when evaluated (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.delta}, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta}). Which constants are recursive is a syntactic property of the declaration. In the erasure relation, a constant that is not an atom erases to its \texttt{tConst} (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.const}) or to any admissible target that the relation's parameter \texttt{rc} gives it (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec}); over a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment, the admissible targets of a constant are the \texttt{tFix} stored as its body (\texttt{EraseProof.RecIn}). They stand for the self-references of a block member's value once \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix} has unfolded the member, where \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} relates a PCUIC \texttt{tFix} to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{tFix} of erased bodies. In the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment, the body of a recursive declaration is a \texttt{tFix} of its whole block (the recursive branch of \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}): member \texttt{j} is named \texttt{Erasure.fixDefName} of the block's \texttt{j}-th declaration, has \texttt{rarg = 0}, and unfolds by \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix} to an erasure of that declaration's Lean value in the empty context, with the fixpoints stored in the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment as the targets of recursive constants (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} relates each body of a PCUIC \texttt{tFix} to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body under the fixpoint's own binders (\texttt{fix\_\allowbreak{}context mfix}). \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased} asks that every fixpoint the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment stores at the kername of a declaration of the evaluation environment erase that declaration (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}; for a recursive declaration, such a block), with bodies whose dependencies are erased: the part of \texttt{globals\_\allowbreak{}erased\_\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}deps} about constants whose \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body is a \texttt{tFix}. The substitution lemmas take the closedness of the admissible targets as a hypothesis (\texttt{EraseProof.RcClosed}), and \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} the closedness of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment (\texttt{hlc : LenvClosed lenv}), where MetaRocq's statements take neither.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Lean's \texttt{Expr} has no fixpoint node: a recursive Lean definition is a constant whose value mentions itself, a member of a block (rule \texttt{block} of \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}, whose values are translated in the model that contains the block). The eraser compiles a declaration to a member of a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{tFix} exactly when it is not a single declaration whose value does not mention its own name (\texttt{name\_\allowbreak{}occurs} in \texttt{visitMutual}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}) and is not remapped to an axiom (DV-12), and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} has fixpoint values only for these blocks. For the source semantics to be simulated, the constants it treats as fixpoints must be exactly these, so the split is the eraser's test, which \texttt{EraseProof.RecursiveDecl} states on the declaration. In a block member's value, the members are constants; in the member's \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body, which the eraser closes into a \texttt{tFix} (\texttt{mkDef}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}) and \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix} unfolds, they are the block's \texttt{tFix} terms. No rule of \texttt{erases} relates a constant to a \texttt{tFix}, so the relation needs \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec}, and \texttt{EraseProof.RecIn} ties its targets to what the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment stores. That stored \texttt{tFix} is not the erasure of a subterm of the source term, so when the source unfolds a recursive constant (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.fixApp}) and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} unfolds the fixpoint (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix}), the relation between the member's Lean value and its unfolded \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body can only come from the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment: \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock} states it, and \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased} gives it for every stored fixpoint, as \texttt{globals\_\allowbreak{}erased\_\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}deps} gives erased bodies for \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta}. The \texttt{fixApp} case of the simulation (\texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}fixApp}) reads it there (\texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased.unfold}): the head's \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value is \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} or the stored \texttt{tFix}, never a \texttt{tConst} (\texttt{EraseProof.LBEval.ne\_\allowbreak{}const}), and the \texttt{tFix} unfolds by \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} with \texttt{rarg = 0} and no earlier arguments, where the reference's \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} case takes the unfolded body from \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix}. In the \texttt{fixAtom} case (\texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}fixAtom}), a recursive constant erased to its \texttt{tConst} evaluates by \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} to the stored \texttt{tFix}, its value in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}, which \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec} relates to the constant, the source's value. A non-recursive constant that \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec} relates to a \texttt{tFix} stored at its kername needs it too: the dependencies of that \texttt{tFix} (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps.fix}) do not lead back to the constant's declaration, so the \ensuremath{\delta} case of the simulation (\texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}delta}) reads the declaration's erasure from \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased}. For the same reason the relation says nothing about the free indices of a target of \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec}: substituting into an erased body leaves a stored \texttt{tFix} unchanged only if it is closed, and the \ensuremath{\beta} and \ensuremath{\zeta} cases of the simulation (\texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}beta}, \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}zeta}) substitute into erased bodies that may contain stored fixpoints. The \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment determines the targets, so their closedness is a property of that environment.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} unfolding recursive constants when evaluated, as the others: it matches \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{tFix} only when each member's value is a \ensuremath{\lambda}, so that one unfolding reaches a value; it would need a shipping change that \ensuremath{\eta}-expands members whose value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}, which the theorem does not need (spec \S{}5.1). In the relation, relating a constant only to its \texttt{tConst}, as \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst} does: the unfolded \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body of a block member, which \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} evaluates, has the block's \texttt{tFix} terms where the member's Lean value has constants, so no erasure would relate the two. In the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment, relating the members' bodies under the fixpoint's binders, as \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} does: a member's Lean value has no binders for the block, and refers to the members as constants. Deriving the closedness of the stored fixpoints from \texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased}, as MetaRocq derives \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} from the erasure of the environment: the closedness of an erasure (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.closed}) itself assumes closed targets (\texttt{EraseProof.RcClosed}), which, for a fixpoint whose bodies refer to the fixpoint itself, is the statement to be derived.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-8}{DV-8}}\label{reg:dv-8}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Deps.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock}: each member of a recursive block unfolds to an erasure of its Lean value, whatever the shape of that value; the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} bodies are those the eraser emits, not \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122-127}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), whose premises include \texttt{isLambda (dbody d)} and \texttt{E.isLambda (E.dbody d')}; Letouzey \S{}4, the \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion of fixpoint bodies (arity control).
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock} has no premise that a member's Lean value or its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body is a \ensuremath{\lambda}, and it relates the bodies as the shipping eraser emits them: a member whose value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda} has a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body that is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} recursive constants in scope may have values that are not \ensuremath{\lambda}s: Lean accepts \texttt{unsafe def ug : CN.\{0\} \ensuremath{\to} CN.\{0\} := (fun \_\allowbreak{} n =\textgreater{} n) (fun x =\textgreater{} ug x)} (corpus \texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}corpus/\allowbreak{}UnsafeRec.lean}), lean4lean's model types it (rule \texttt{block} of \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}), and the shipping eraser erases the value as it is (\texttt{visitMutual}, \texttt{mkDef}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}; SHIPPING-CHANGES R-11). With the \texttt{isLambda} premises, no block containing such a member would be related to its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} image, and the theorem would exclude these inputs.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} requiring \ensuremath{\lambda}-bodied members, which excludes in-scope inputs; \ensuremath{\eta}-expanding non-\ensuremath{\lambda} members in the shipping eraser, which changes their output and which the theorem does not need (spec \S{}5.1).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-9}{DV-9}}\label{reg:dv-9}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases}, the correctness of the outputs of the shipping \texttt{Erasure.erasePure} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}): the output term is an erasure of the input (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases}) with erased dependencies (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps}), in a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment with erased blocks (\texttt{EraseProof.BlocksErased}) and closed bodies (\texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed}); the theorem says nothing about \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion. The environment stores a recursive constant as the bare fixpoint \texttt{tFix defs j} of its erased block (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesBlock}), with \texttt{rarg = 0} and the members' erased values as the bodies.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{expanded} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpandedFix.v:33}) and \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}eprogram} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpandedFix.v:187}), which MetaRocq proves of the outputs of its erasure on \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded inputs (\texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}erase}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:1903}; \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}erase\_\allowbreak{}global}, \texttt{:1922}) and which its switch from guarded to unguarded fixpoint evaluation takes as a precondition, through \texttt{isEtaExp} (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}opt\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}target}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpandedFix.v:1684}); the well-formedness of \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoints, whose bodies are \ensuremath{\lambda}s (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWellformed.v:163}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the outputs of \texttt{Erasure.erasePure} are not \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}eprogram} in general, and \texttt{EraseProof.erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases} does not claim it. A constant body that is a bare \texttt{tFix} is never \texttt{expanded}: \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}tFix} needs \texttt{args \textless{}\textgreater{} []} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpandedFix.v:51}) and \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}mkApps} excludes fixpoint heads (\texttt{:39}; also \texttt{isEtaExp\_\allowbreak{}tFix}, \texttt{:1504}). A member whose Lean value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda} has a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body that is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}, which \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}tFix} and the well-formedness of fixpoints reject; \texttt{peregrine validate} rejects such an output (SHIPPING-CHANGES R-11).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Lean has no fixpoint term: recursion lives in constants, which the shipping eraser emits as bare \texttt{tFix} blocks stored as the constants' bodies (DV-7), and it erases a member's value as it is (DV-8). An \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}eprogram} output needs a shipping change (\ensuremath{\eta}-expanding recursive constants at their use sites, and members whose value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}), and shipping changes are made only when strictly necessary (spec \S{}5.1): the theorem is about \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation (\texttt{EraseProof.LBEval}, \texttt{eval}), of which expansion is no premise. MetaRocq needs expansion to switch fixpoint evaluation to the unguarded rules; with \texttt{rarg = 0}, which every emitted fixpoint has, the guarded rule \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:171}) has the premises of the unguarded \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix'} (\texttt{:189}), and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix\_\allowbreak{}value} (\texttt{:180}) never applies.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\eta}-expanding in the shipping eraser, at the use sites of recursive constants and in members whose value is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}: a shipping change that no statement needs (the gap is recorded as SHIPPING-CHANGES R-11); stating \texttt{expanded\_\allowbreak{}eprogram} of the output, which is false on the eraser's outputs.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-10}{DV-10}}\label{reg:dv-10}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}EvalEnv.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}, the constants the source semantics unfolds: it returns the value of a definition or theorem and nothing for an opaque constant.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the \ensuremath{\delta} rule of PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:247}; MetaCoq paper \S{}5.6), which unfolds every constant whose declaration has a body (\texttt{cst\_\allowbreak{}body decl = Some body}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean \texttt{opaque} declaration (\texttt{ConstantInfo.opaqueInfo}) has a value, but \texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?} does not return it, so evaluation does not unfold the constant. The shipping eraser emits the opaque's value as the body of its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant (\texttt{ci.value? (allowOpaque := true)} in \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), so \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation unfolds what the source semantics leaves stuck.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} lean4lean's model gives an opaque constant no defining equation (rule \texttt{opaque} of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Environment/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:164-169}, adds the constant only), and \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} follows it; so unfolding an opaque is not a definitional equality of the model. The proof relates each evaluation of the source to a typed definitional equality of the model (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.defeq}, subject reduction); for a \ensuremath{\delta} step, \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv.unfold} gives it for definitions (their defining equation) and theorems (their type is a proposition, so proof irrelevance equates them with their value), and nothing gives it for opaques, whose type need not be a proposition.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} unfolding opaques as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} does: evaluation steps would no longer be definitional equalities of the model, and type preservation fails for terms whose type depends on an opaque's value (with \texttt{opaque c : T := t} and an axiom \texttt{f : (x : T) \ensuremath{\to} F x}, \texttt{f c : F c} evaluates to \texttt{f t : F t}, and the model does not equate \texttt{F c} with \texttt{F t}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-11}{DV-11}}\label{reg:dv-11}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Atoms.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom}, with \texttt{EraseProof.arityShape}, \texttt{EraseProof.EvidentZero}, \texttt{EraseProof.DeltaFree} and \texttt{EraseProof.EvidentProp}; \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}, the rule \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom} and the values \texttt{EraseProof.AtomSpine} (in \texttt{EraseProof.SrcValue.spine}): the constants without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule that are values of the source semantics; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, the premise \texttt{ac c = false} of the rules \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.const} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec} of \texttt{EraseProof.Erases}, whose parameter \texttt{ac} is the atom test: atoms erase only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Atoms.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.atomSpine\_\allowbreak{}box}: an erasure of an atom spine that is a result of \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation is \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's atoms \texttt{atom} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:51}), which contain the inductive types \texttt{tInd} and the constructors \texttt{tConstruct}; \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}atom} (\texttt{:331}) evaluates them to themselves, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}app\_\allowbreak{}cong} (\texttt{:311}) evaluates their applications, and \texttt{value} (\texttt{:500}) lists the results; a constant without a body has no rule (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta}, \texttt{:247}, needs \texttt{cst\_\allowbreak{}body decl = Some body}). On the erasure side, \texttt{erases} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}) relates every constant to its \texttt{tConst} (\texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst}, \texttt{:104}), has no rule for \texttt{tInd}, which erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} (\texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}box}, \texttt{:140}), and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConstruct} (\texttt{:106}) requires the inductive not to be propositional (\texttt{isPropositional}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:109}, which reads the inductive's declared arity syntactically: \texttt{isPropositionalArity}, \texttt{:103}, with \texttt{destArity}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICAst.v:486}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule in the source semantics is a value when its declared type is evidently an arity (\texttt{EraseProof.arityShape}: syntactically \texttt{\ensuremath{\Pi} x\ensuremath{_1}\ldots{}x\ensuremath{_n}, Sort u}) or evidently a proposition (\texttt{EraseProof.EvidentProp}): a \ensuremath{\Pi}-telescope over an application \texttt{h.\{vs\} a\ensuremath{_1}\ldots{}a\ensuremath{_n}} whose head \texttt{h} is an axiom or an opaque constant (\texttt{EraseProof.DeltaFree}) with declared type a syntactic arity \texttt{\ensuremath{\Pi} y\ensuremath{_1}\ldots{}y\ensuremath{_n}, Sort u} of exactly \texttt{n} binders, and whose sort at that occurrence, \texttt{u} with \texttt{h}'s level parameters instantiated by \texttt{vs} (\texttt{Erasure.Pure.instLevel}), is evidently zero (\texttt{EraseProof.EvidentZero}). Such a constant evaluates to itself (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom}), and the applications it heads are values (\texttt{EraseProof.AtomSpine}). Atomhood is a property of the constant, decided on declared types, not on the levels of an occurrence: a proof \texttt{hq.\{v\} : P.\{v\}} (with \texttt{axiom P.\{v\} : Sort v}) whose propositionality depends on its own level parameter is not an atom, not even at \texttt{hq.\{0\}}. Every other constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule is stuck. In the erasure relation, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst} becomes \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.const} with the premise that the constant is not an atom (\texttt{ac c = false}, where \texttt{ac} is the atom test), and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.constRec} has the same premise: an atom erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.box}), as \texttt{tInd} does.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the fragment has no inductive types (DV-6), so its base types and the canonical proofs of atomic propositions are axioms; without a rule that makes them values, no program that instantiates a polymorphic function at a base type or passes such a proof by value evaluates, and the correctness theorem says nothing about it. With the rule, the programs \texttt{(fun (\ensuremath{\alpha} : Type) (x : \ensuremath{\alpha}) =\textgreater{} x) A}, \texttt{(fun (h : P) (y : Type) =\textgreater{} y) hP} and \texttt{(fun (h : P.\{0\}) (x : A) =\textgreater{} x) hp} (with \texttt{axiom P.\{v\} : Sort v}, \texttt{axiom hp : P.\{0\}}) evaluate through \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom} on \texttt{A}, \texttt{hP} and \texttt{hp}, and \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} applies to them with every hypothesis a checked term (\texttt{EraseProof.Test.NV5.inst}, \texttt{EraseProof.Test.NV6.inst}, \texttt{EraseProof.Test.NV7.inst}). The class is syntactic ("evident") because the eraser must box each atom from the declared types alone, without a typing hypothesis, and on this class it provably does: on an atom spine the oracle never answers "keep" (\texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}atom}, \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Atom.lean}, whose level test is \texttt{EraseProof.EvidentZero} by \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.alwaysZero\_\allowbreak{}eq}); a semantic class (every erasable constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule) would need the eraser's oracle \texttt{Erasure.Pure.isErasable} to box all of them, which needs canonicity (no neutral term is definitionally equal to a sort), and lean4lean \texttt{master} does not prove it. The head is \texttt{EraseProof.DeltaFree} because the head of a propositional constructor's type is an inductive type, which never \ensuremath{\delta}-reduces: a proof whose proposition is headed by a definition that unfolds to a \ensuremath{\Pi} can be applied, and the oracle then answers from the arguments' types (with \texttt{axiom hq : Q}, \texttt{def Q : Prop := \ensuremath{\forall} P : Prop, P \ensuremath{\to} P}, \texttt{axiom A : Type} and \texttt{axiom a : A}, it keeps the ill-typed spine \texttt{hq A a}: \texttt{EraseProof.Test.Atoms.defHead\_\allowbreak{}kept}), so \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}atom}, which has no typing hypothesis, fails for such heads. The head's sort is read at the occurrence because a Lean level can be \texttt{0}, whereas \texttt{isPropositional} reads an inductive's declared sort, which no Rocq universe instance turns into \texttt{Prop}. Atomhood does not depend on the occurrence because the eraser erases a universe-polymorphic body once, at its level parameters, where the oracle keeps the level-dependent proof \texttt{hq.\{v\}} (it boxes \texttt{hq.\{0\}}: \texttt{EraseProof.Test.Atoms.levelDependent\_\allowbreak{}kept}): were \texttt{hq.\{0\}} a value, a body passing \texttt{hq.\{v\}}, evaluated at level \texttt{0}, would reach a value in the source while its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} image is stuck on the axiom \texttt{hq}, and erasure would not commute with level instantiation, which \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}subst\_\allowbreak{}instance\_\allowbreak{}decl} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureProperties.v:412}) states and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.instLevels} proves (the relation's atom test \texttt{ac} reads a constant's name, not its levels). An atom is a value of the source semantics, while no rule of \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation returns a \texttt{tConst}: the erasure of an atom that is the result of an evaluation must be the result of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation, so it cannot be a \texttt{tConst}; it is \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}, which \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} has for \texttt{tInd} too.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} every constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule stuck (the theorem then says nothing about the programs above); a semantic class (needs canonicity); heads that are definitions (the oracle keeps proofs with such heads, above); heads that \ensuremath{\delta}-reduce to an \texttt{EraseProof.DeltaFree} head (further from the reference, and the eraser's boxing of the class would have to follow the oracle's \ensuremath{\delta} steps through definitions); the head's declared sort instead of its sort at the occurrence (leaves proofs of \texttt{P.\{0\}}, with \texttt{axiom P.\{v\} : Sort v}, stuck with no forcing reason); atomhood decided at each occurrence (makes the theorem false, above); the head's declared type read up to the kernel's \ensuremath{\delta} (the class would no longer be read syntactically, as \texttt{isPropositionalArity} reads the declared arity, and the eraser's boxing of the class would have to follow the oracle's \ensuremath{\delta} steps through definitions; the oracle does box the constants this reading would add, such as \texttt{R} and \texttt{hR} of \texttt{EraseProof.Test.Oracle.irreducibleAlias}); in the relation, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst} for atoms too (an atom that is the result of an evaluation would then erase to a \texttt{tConst}, which is not a result of \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-12}{DV-12}}\label{reg:dv-12}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}EvalEnv.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv} with its field \texttt{axiomatized}, and \texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}: the evaluation environment carries the constants the configuration remaps to foreign code, and evaluation does not unfold them. \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Restrict.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.evalEnvOf}: the evaluation environment of a program, whose remapped constants are those of the shipping eraser's own test \texttt{Erasure.axiomatized} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}): a single declaration that the view marks \texttt{@[extern]}, under the configuration \texttt{extern := .preferAxiom}. \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Deps.lean}, the remapped branch of \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}: a remapped constant, which has a Lean value, is related to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration without a body.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the environment of PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}), whose rule \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{:247}) unfolds a constant exactly when its declaration has a body; and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:264}), which erases a constant with a body to one with a body and a constant without a body to one without.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a definition or theorem for which \texttt{axiomatized} holds has a Lean value but no \ensuremath{\delta} rule in the source semantics: it is stuck, like the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axiom the eraser emits for it. Which constants are remapped is an input of the source semantics, besides the declarations; for a program, \texttt{EraseProof.evalEnvOf} derives it from the configuration and the trusted view's \texttt{isExtern}, exactly as the eraser does. \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl} relates such a constant to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration without a body, a pair for which \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} is \texttt{False}.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} under the configuration \texttt{extern := .preferAxiom} (the default of \texttt{ErasureConfig}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), the shipping eraser emits a declaration tagged \texttt{@[extern]} as a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axiom, although it has a Lean value, so that it is linked with a foreign implementation (Dima \S{}4.2). Neither lean4lean's model nor \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation models that implementation; the source semantics can only leave the constant stuck, as \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation leaves the axiom.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a scope condition excluding programs that mention a remapped constant: it also excludes programs that never evaluate the constant.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-13}{DV-13}}\label{reg:dv-13}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Whnf.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.LocalsOK}: the eraser's locals, a list of free variables with their types and, for a \texttt{let}, their values, related to a lean4lean context \texttt{Lean4Lean.VLCtx} with free-variable entries only; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Agree.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}agree}, with \texttt{EraseProof.ClosedDecls}, \texttt{EraseProof.LocalsSupport} and \texttt{EraseProof.LocalsAgree}: over closed declarations, the erasability oracle answers alike under two lists of locals that agree on the free variables the term reaches through the locals' types and values. With them, \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.hasFVar} and \texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed}: no body stored in the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment contains a free variable; \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}State.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.hasFVar\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}false}: the erasure of a term without free variables has none, so the body of a constant, which \texttt{EraseProof.StateOK.registerDef} stores, has none. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, the rule \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.fvar} of \texttt{EraseProof.Erases}: the erasure relation relates the traversal's free variables to themselves, under a context \texttt{Lean4Lean.VLCtx} whose free-variable entries type them. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Abstract.lean}: \texttt{EraseProof.abstract1}, the shifting abstraction of lean4lean's \texttt{Expr.abstract1} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Axioms.lean:443}) on \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} terms, with \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.uninstantiateN}: closing a binder on both sides keeps the relation, when the admissible targets of recursive constants do not mention the variable (\texttt{EraseProof.RcFresh}); and \texttt{EraseProof.substFVars}, a simultaneous substitution of free variables, with \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.substRc}: substituting free variables on the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} side that the source term does not contain keeps the relation, with the admissible targets substituted. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Glue.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.abstract\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}abstract1}: on a term without loose indices, the traversal's \texttt{abstract} is \texttt{EraseProof.abstract1} at index \texttt{0}. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Frame.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.visit\_\allowbreak{}agree}: over closed declarations, the traversal at the pure backend runs alike under two lists of locals that agree on the free variables the visited term reaches through the locals' types and values; on a closed term, such as a constant's body, it runs alike under any two lists of locals. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Steps.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.CtxOK}: the context invariant of the traversal's correctness proof, whose locals mirror a context of free-variable entries and whose counter allocates only variables fresh for that context; with the steps \texttt{EraseProof.visitExpr\_\allowbreak{}lam\_\allowbreak{}step} and \texttt{EraseProof.visitExpr\_\allowbreak{}letE\_\allowbreak{}step}: a binder's body, opened with a fresh variable and erased, is closed by the traversal's \texttt{abstract}, and a \texttt{let} value is erased under the \texttt{let}'s own local; and \texttt{EraseProof.visitMutual\_\allowbreak{}nonrec\_\allowbreak{}step}: a constant's value is erased under the caller's locals, as in the empty context. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}CloseFix.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix}: \texttt{mkDef}'s closing loop of the traversal's non-shifting \texttt{toBvar}, which turns the fix variable of member \texttt{j} of an \texttt{m}-member block into \texttt{bvar (m-1-j)}; with \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix\_\allowbreak{}closed}: a closed body so closed has no loose index beyond the block's binders; and \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix\_\allowbreak{}substl}: instantiated by the block's fixpoints as \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix} does, the closed body is the body with fix variable \texttt{xs[j]} replaced by \texttt{tFix defs j} (\texttt{EraseProof.fixTargets}), the substitution that \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.substRc} takes. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Block.lean}: the members of a recursive block are erased with fresh fix variables as the members' admissible targets (\texttt{EraseProof.rcBlock}, \texttt{EraseProof.body\_\allowbreak{}step}), \texttt{mkDef} closes each erased body by \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix} (\texttt{EraseProof.mkDef\_\allowbreak{}run}), and the stored block has no free variable (\texttt{EraseProof.closeFix\_\allowbreak{}hasFVar}); \texttt{EraseProof.block\_\allowbreak{}finish} turns the fix variables into the registered fixpoints by \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix\_\allowbreak{}substl} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.substRc}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's erasure function \texttt{erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:989}) and erasure relation \texttt{erases} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.2--\S{}7.3, Figs. 17--18), which work on de Bruijn indices under a context \texttt{\ensuremath{\Gamma}} of typed binders (rule \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tRel}, \texttt{:89}; named variables occur only in \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tVar}, \texttt{:90}, and typed terms contain none); and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1309}), which erases a constant's body in the empty context; the rule \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122}), which relates the bodies of a \texttt{tFix} de Bruijn, under the fixpoint's binders, and \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:238}), which instantiates them with \texttt{fix\_\allowbreak{}subst} (\texttt{:210}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the erasure is locally nameless. Under a binder, the term is opened with a fresh free variable, recorded with its type (and, for a \texttt{let}, its value) in a list of locals, and the erased body is closed again by turning that variable into a bound variable. The oracle runs on open terms under these locals, not under a context of de Bruijn binders; \texttt{EraseProof.LocalsOK} gives the locals their meaning in the model. A constant's body is erased under the locals of the place where the traversal first meets the constant, not in the empty context: \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}agree} equates the oracle's answers under the two, since a declaration's body is closed (\texttt{EraseProof.ClosedDecls}) and so reaches no local, and \texttt{EraseProof.visit\_\allowbreak{}agree} equates the traversal's runs on the body. A \texttt{let} value is erased under the \texttt{let}'s own local, not in the outer context; \texttt{EraseProof.visit\_\allowbreak{}agree} equates the runs under the two, since the value does not mention that local. The erasure relation is stated on these open terms: a free variable erases to itself (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.fvar}, MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tVar}, which applies to no typed term there), and where the relation judges erasability (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasableS}), the free-variable entries of the lean4lean context give these variables their types. Closing a binder is stated with the shifting abstraction, the inverse of the source side's opening \texttt{Expr.instantiate1'} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Axioms.lean:404}), as lean4lean states it for its translation (\texttt{Lean4Lean.TrExprS.uninstantiateN}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Lemmas.lean:2132}), not with the traversal's non-shifting \texttt{abstract}. The members of a recursive block refer to each other by free variables while they are erased; replacing these by the block's fixpoints (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases.substRc}) turns the targets of the block's constants into the stored \texttt{tFix}. The stored bodies are closed by \texttt{mkDef}'s loop of non-shifting \texttt{toBvar} steps (\texttt{EraseProof.closeFix}), not built under the fixpoint's binders; \texttt{EraseProof.closeFix\_\allowbreak{}substl} shows that \texttt{cunfold\_\allowbreak{}fix}'s instantiation of such a body is that replacement. It is stated for the loop as a whole, since the loop's later steps abstract at indices above \texttt{0}, which \texttt{EraseProof.abstract\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}abstract1} (the traversal's \texttt{abstract}, at index \texttt{0}) does not cover.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the shipping eraser (spec \S{}2), whose traversal is written this way: \texttt{withLocalDecl} and \texttt{withLocalDef} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}) open a binder with a fresh free variable pushed onto the locals, the oracle is called with these locals, \texttt{abstract} and \texttt{toBvar} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}) close the erased body, \texttt{mkDef} closes the members of a block of mutual definitions, which the traversal refers to by free variables, \texttt{visitLet} erases a \texttt{let}'s value after pushing the \texttt{let}'s local, and \texttt{visitMutual} erases a constant's body without resetting the caller's locals.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a de Bruijn rewrite of the traversal, a large shipping change that no output needs (spec \S{}5.1 allows only strictly necessary shipping changes); resetting the locals in \texttt{visitMutual}, or visiting a \texttt{let} value before pushing the \texttt{let}'s local, shipping changes that the frame lemmas \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}agree} and \texttt{EraseProof.visit\_\allowbreak{}agree} make unnecessary; stating the binder lemma with the traversal's non-shifting \texttt{abstract}, which undoes the opening only on terms without loose indices beyond the variable's depth, a condition the lemma would then need as an extra hypothesis.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-14}{DV-14}}\label{reg:dv-14}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Deps.lean}, the rule \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps.const} of \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps}: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant \texttt{tConst (toKername c)} has erased dependencies when \texttt{c} is a declaration of the evaluation environment whose \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration at \texttt{toKername c} erases it (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}) and whose \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body, if any, has erased dependencies; the rule is indexed by the source constant \texttt{c}, not by the kername. And \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Restrict.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.KernameInj}: the declarations of the evaluation environment have distinct kernames, the hypothesis \texttt{hinj} of \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} and of its \ensuremath{\delta} and \texttt{fixAtom} cases (\texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}delta}, \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}fixAtom}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}deps\_\allowbreak{}tConst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:324-329}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.4, p. 8:64), where the PCUIC declaration and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration are found at the same kername \texttt{kn}, the name of the \texttt{tConst}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean names become \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} kernames through \texttt{toKername} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}), so a Lean constant and its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant have different names, and the rule relates the declaration of \texttt{c} to the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration at \texttt{toKername c}. When two declarations of the evaluation environment have the same kername, the rule may justify the same \texttt{tConst} by either. The simulation therefore takes injectivity of \texttt{toKername} on the evaluation environment's declarations as a hypothesis (\texttt{EraseProof.KernameInj}): with it, the declaration that \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps.const} names for the \texttt{tConst} of a constant is that constant's own, as the shared \texttt{kn} guarantees in the reference.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the shipping eraser names the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant of \texttt{c} by \texttt{toKername c} (\texttt{visitMutual}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), and \texttt{toKername} is not injective: the escaping of \texttt{cleanIdent} and the numeric name components make distinct names coincide (SHIPPING-CHANGES R-3). So a kername does not determine the source declaration, and the rule names the declaration it uses. The eraser's dependency collection rejects programs whose collected declarations share a kername (\texttt{findCollision}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Collect.lean}; SHIPPING-CHANGES S-18), so the ambiguity does not arise on the declarations it erases, \texttt{EraseProof.KernameInj} states that check, and \texttt{EraseProof.collectDeps\_\allowbreak{}spec} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core/\allowbreak{}Collect.lean}) proves it of every successful run.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} an injective mangling, a shipping change that alters the bytes of every name with special characters and that the theorem does not need (spec \S{}5.1); \texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps} over all declarations of the program rather than the evaluation environment, which fails when two constants of the program outside the dependency closure share a kername.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-15}{DV-15}}\label{reg:dv-15}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Relation/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}, the rules \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.lam} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.letE} of \texttt{EraseProof.Erases}: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} binder of a Lean binder with user name \texttt{n} is named \texttt{Erasure.binderNameOf n}, the shipping eraser's naming (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLambda} and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:93}, \texttt{:96}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), which give the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} binder the PCUIC binder's own name, \texttt{na.(binder\_\allowbreak{}name)}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean binder name is a hierarchical \texttt{Name}, a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} binder name is anonymous or a string (\texttt{BinderName}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}). \texttt{Erasure.binderNameOf n} is the string \texttt{n.toString} when each of its characters is printable ASCII (codes 33 to 126), and anonymous otherwise: binders named \texttt{x} and \texttt{a.b} keep their names, binders named \texttt{\ensuremath{\alpha}\ensuremath{_1}} or \texttt{\ensuremath{\langle\!\langle}a b\ensuremath{\rangle\!\rangle}} become anonymous.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the relation describes the output of the shipping eraser (spec \S{}2), which names binders by \texttt{Erasure.binderNameOf}: peregrine's \texttt{.ast} format admits non-ASCII characters only inside string literals, and names are bare atoms (peregrine-tool \texttt{doc/\allowbreak{}format.md}, lines 12 and 68-69). Lean's and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s names have different types, so some conversion is needed where MetaRocq needs none (PCUIC and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} share \texttt{name}).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} binder names left unconstrained in \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.lam} and \texttt{EraseProof.Erases.letE}: the relation would no longer describe the names the eraser prints, and it would depart further from \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLambda}, which fixes the name; keeping every Lean name, a shipping change whose output peregrine rejects.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-16}{DV-16}}\label{reg:dv-16}

\begin{itemize}
