\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval}, \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} weak call-by-value evaluation, with its atoms \texttt{EraseProof.lbAtom}, stated on the shipping AST \texttt{LBTerm} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}); with it the functions \texttt{EraseProof.csubst}, \texttt{EraseProof.closedn}, \texttt{EraseProof.hasFVar} and the environment condition \texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:119}) on the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} terms \texttt{term} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EAst.v:29}), with \texttt{atom} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:36}), \texttt{csubst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ECSubst.v:14}), \texttt{closedn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ELiftSubst.v:90}) and \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}); MetaCoq paper \S{}7.1 (Fig. 16 and the amended evaluation rules, p. 8:60).
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{LBTerm} has no \texttt{tVar}, \texttt{tEvar}, \texttt{tCoFix}, \texttt{tLazy} or \texttt{tForce}, and its only primitive values are 63-bit integers. So \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval} has no rules \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}cofix\_\allowbreak{}case} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:198}), \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}cofix\_\allowbreak{}proj} (\texttt{:205}) or \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}force} (\texttt{:279}), its rule \texttt{prim} (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}prim}, \texttt{:275}) evaluates an integer to itself, and \texttt{EraseProof.lbAtom} has no case for \texttt{tCoFix} or \texttt{tLazy}. \texttt{LBTerm} has a constructor that \texttt{term} lacks, \texttt{fvar}, a free variable named by a Lean \texttt{FVarId}: \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval} has no rule for it, \texttt{EraseProof.csubst} leaves it unchanged and \texttt{EraseProof.closedn} counts it as closed, as MetaRocq's \texttt{csubst} and \texttt{closedn} treat \texttt{tVar}; \texttt{EraseProof.hasFVar} tests whether it occurs, and has no MetaRocq counterpart; \texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed} requires, besides the closedness of \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env}, that no body stored in the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment contains a free variable. The rules for constructors in block form, \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}block} (\texttt{:151}), \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}proj\_\allowbreak{}block} (\texttt{:228}) and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}construct\_\allowbreak{}block} (\texttt{:254}), are absent; each requires the flag \texttt{with\_\allowbreak{}constructor\_\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}block} to be true, which it is not in \texttt{default\_\allowbreak{}wcbv\_\allowbreak{}flags} (\texttt{:69}), the flags of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}). At flags where that flag is false, \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval} has exactly the rules of \texttt{eval} whose term constructors \texttt{LBTerm} has.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the shipping eraser (spec \S{}2), whose output is an \texttt{LBTerm}, the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} that peregrine reads; evaluation is stated on that type. The terms without a constructor in \texttt{LBTerm} cannot occur in the eraser's output, so their rules have nothing to apply to. The constructor \texttt{fvar} is part of the shipping AST because the traversal is locally nameless (DV-13): it opens binders with free variables and closes them with \texttt{abstract} and \texttt{toBvar} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}) before a body is stored, which \texttt{EraseProof.LenvClosed} records. MetaRocq's erasure works on de Bruijn indices and maps \texttt{tVar} only to \texttt{tVar} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:996}), which typed terms do not contain (PCUIC's typing has no rule for it), so \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} needs no such clause. The block rules cannot fire at the flags of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct}, at which the simulation evaluates; results stated for every flag, such as \texttt{EraseProof.LBEval.eq\_\allowbreak{}box\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}headOf}, are about the relation without them.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} extending \texttt{LBTerm} with the missing constructors, a shipping change that no output of the eraser needs (spec \S{}5.1 allows only strictly necessary shipping changes); stating evaluation on a separate transcription of \texttt{term} reached through a translation from \texttt{LBTerm}, which every statement would pass through and which would still need an image for \texttt{fvar}; including the block rules, which the statements never use at their flags.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-17}{DV-17}}\label{reg:dv-17}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}sound}, with \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isArity\_\allowbreak{}sound}, and the soundness of the steps they rest on, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.inferType\_\allowbreak{}sound} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Infer.lean}) and \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.whnf\_\allowbreak{}sound} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Whnf.lean}): the eraser's erasability oracle \texttt{Erasure.Pure.isErasable} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}) and its type inference, weak-head reduction and arity test run with fuel, and these theorems state the soundness of their results for every fuel, about the runs that return a result. The traversal that erases a term is fuelled in the same way: \texttt{EraseProof.erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Core.lean}) is about a run of \texttt{Erasure.erasePure} that returns a program, and is proved by induction on the traversal's fuel (\texttt{EraseProof.traversal\_\allowbreak{}spec}). The final theorem \texttt{EraseProof.erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Main.lean}) is partial correctness: it is about a run of the entry point of \texttt{\#erase}, \texttt{Erasure.eraseEntry} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Entry.lean}), that returns a program (its hypothesis \texttt{hrun}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's erasability test \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:894}) and erasure function \texttt{erase} (\texttt{:989}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.2, Fig. 17): total functions, whose reductions terminate by well-founded recursion under the hypothesis \texttt{normalization\_\allowbreak{}in} that every well-typed term of every well-formed environment related to the abstract one is strongly normalizing (\texttt{NormalizationIn}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSN.v:44}; a parameter of \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} and of the section of \texttt{erase}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:969}); the correctness of \texttt{erase}, \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1228}), takes the same hypothesis and holds for every input, and so does the correctness of the erasure of a program, \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), about \texttt{erase} and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}global\_\allowbreak{}deps}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the oracle's functions recurse on a fuel argument and fail with the error \texttt{fuel} when it runs out (\texttt{Erasure.EraseError}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Collect.lean}); on the eraser's path the fuel of an oracle call is \texttt{Erasure.oracleFuel}. No statement has a normalization hypothesis. The soundness theorems hold for every fuel and speak only about a run that returns (\texttt{Pure.isErasable cx fuel ls e = .ok true} in \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}sound}): a run that exhausts its fuel gives no answer and carries no guarantee, and on the eraser's path it is an error of \texttt{\#erase}, never an output. The eraser's other computations, the dependency collection (\texttt{Erasure.collectFuel}) and the traversal (\texttt{Erasure.travFuel}, \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}), are fuelled in the same way. \texttt{EraseProof.erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} assumes that \texttt{Erasure.eraseEntry} returns a program and says nothing about a run that fails; on an input in scope such a run, for example one that exhausts a fuel, is an error of \texttt{\#erase} (\texttt{erasure failed: \ldots{}}), never an output.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} lean4lean \texttt{master} proves no normalization theorem for its typing, and the spec (\S{}2) excludes hypotheses that stand in for results lean4lean lacks; a normalization hypothesis would be one. It would also be false in the fragment: the model gives a recursive unsafe constant its defining equation (rule \texttt{block} of \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}), so a well-typed term such as \texttt{loop a}, with \texttt{unsafe def loop : A \ensuremath{\to} A := fun x =\textgreater{} loop x} (DV-22), reduces to itself by \ensuremath{\delta} and \ensuremath{\beta} and is not strongly normalizing. Such terms also occur in the types the oracle reduces (with \texttt{unsafe def L : Type \ensuremath{\to} Type := fun x =\textgreater{} L x}, the type \texttt{L A}), so on inputs in scope the oracle's reductions need not terminate, and only a bound on them, such as fuel, makes the oracle a total function.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a normalization hypothesis, as MetaRocq's \texttt{normalization\_\allowbreak{}in}: a stand-in for a theorem lean4lean \texttt{master} lacks (spec \S{}2), and false in the fragment (above); a total oracle defined by well-founded recursion, which needs that normalization theorem to be defined at all.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-18}{DV-18}}\label{reg:dv-18}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}sound}, with \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isArity\_\allowbreak{}sound} and \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.alwaysZero\_\allowbreak{}sound}, and the soundness of the steps they rest on, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.inferType\_\allowbreak{}sound} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Infer.lean}) and \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.whnf\_\allowbreak{}sound} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Whnf.lean}), and, on atom spines, \texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}atom} (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Oracle/\allowbreak{}Atom.lean}): the eraser decides erasability with its own oracle, the shipping \texttt{Erasure.Pure.isErasable} (\texttt{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}), with its type inference \texttt{Erasure.Pure.inferType}, its weak-head reduction \texttt{Erasure.Pure.whnf}, its arity test \texttt{Erasure.Pure.isArity} and its level test \texttt{Erasure.Pure.alwaysZero}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:894}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.2, Fig. 17), which decides erasability with MetaRocq's verified type checker: it infers a type with \texttt{type\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}typing} (\texttt{safechecker/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSafeRetyping.v:806}), tests it with \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}arity} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:784}), and otherwise reduces the type's type to a sort and tests it with \texttt{Sort.is\_\allowbreak{}propositional} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Universes.v:1528}); \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableP} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:915}) proves that it reflects \texttt{isErasable} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:18}) in both directions. Its reductions unfold every constant with a body (\texttt{hnf}, \texttt{safechecker/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSafeReduce.v:1839}, at \texttt{RedFlags.default}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICNormal.v:26}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the oracle is an infer-only retyping procedure of the eraser itself, with fuel, over the program's declarations and the eraser's locals: it infers a type of the term, answers "erasable" if that type reduces to an arity, and otherwise reduces the type's type to a sort and answers "erasable" exactly when the sort is structurally \texttt{\ensuremath{\approx} 0}. Only the \texttt{true} direction of \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableP} is proved: an "erasable" answer gives \texttt{EraseProof.ErasableS} (\texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}sound}). There is no general completeness: the oracle may answer "keep" on an erasable term, except on the atom spines of DV-11, where it answers "erasable" or fails (\texttt{EraseProof.Pure.isErasable\_\allowbreak{}atom}), and it fails, with an error and no answer, when its fuel runs out (DV-17) or a type does not reduce to a \ensuremath{\Pi} or a sort. Its reductions unfold every definition, as those of \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} do, whatever the elaborator attribute \texttt{@[irreducible]} says: on an environment whose aliases \texttt{IProp : Type := Prop} and \texttt{Endo : Type := A \ensuremath{\to} A} are \texttt{@[irreducible]} in Lean, it types \texttt{fun (\_\allowbreak{} : R) (x : A) =\textgreater{} x} and \texttt{fI a} and keeps them, and it boxes \texttt{R : IProp} and the proof \texttt{hR : R} (\texttt{EraseProof.Test.Oracle.irreducibleAlias}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the verified checker available for Lean is lean4lean's, and its soundness carries debts that the fragment does not need. Every soundness theorem of lean4lean's type checker goes through \texttt{Methods.withFuel.WF} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}TypeChecker.lean:48}), which reaches the \texttt{sorry} lemmas of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrProj} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}Expr.lean:68}), the projection, recursor and \ensuremath{\eta}-structure sorries \texttt{reduceProjCore.WF} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}TypeChecker/\allowbreak{}Reduce.lean:143}), \texttt{reduceRecursor.WF} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}TypeChecker/\allowbreak{}WHNF.lean:6}), \texttt{inferProj.WF} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}TypeChecker/\allowbreak{}InferType.lean:388}), \texttt{tryEtaStructCore.WF} and \texttt{isDefEqUnitLike.WF} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}TypeChecker/\allowbreak{}IsDefEq.lean:225,486}), the strengthening sorry \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.IsDefEqU.weakN\_\allowbreak{}iff} (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Typing/\allowbreak{}UniqueTyping.lean:172}), and the axioms of \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Axioms.lean} (the pure meaning of \texttt{Expr.instantiate1}, \texttt{Expr.abstract}, \texttt{Level.normalize} and others) together with \texttt{bv\_\allowbreak{}decide} axioms. MetaRocq's \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} rests on a checker without such debts. The soundness of the eraser's own oracle reaches only lean4lean's sorries L1--L5, which the simulation needs anyway. General completeness would need canonicity (no neutral term is convertible to a sort or a \ensuremath{\Pi}), which lean4lean \texttt{master} does not prove, and the correctness theorem needs only soundness.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} lean4lean's checker on the eraser's path (the debts above); reductions that skip \texttt{@[irreducible]} in the arity and sort tests, as Lean's \texttt{Meta} does at default transparency: the oracle would keep the proof \texttt{hR : R} of \texttt{R : IProp}, as the \texttt{Meta} path does (\texttt{doc/\allowbreak{}SHIPPING-CHANGES.md}, R-14), a further divergence from \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} with no forcing reason; skipping \texttt{@[irreducible]} in type inference too: the oracle then fails on \texttt{fun (\_\allowbreak{} : R) (x : A) =\textgreater{} x}, whose domain has a sort only through \texttt{IProp}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-19}{DV-19}}\label{reg:dv-19}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Main.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.erase\_\allowbreak{}correct}, the final theorem about \texttt{\#erase}: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value of the emitted term is related to the source value by the erasure relation \texttt{EraseProof.Erases}, and no first-order corollary is stated.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's first-order results (MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, p. 8:63): \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}firstorder} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2310}), which, for a closed term whose type is a first-order inductive type (\texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}ind}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:67}) in an axiom-free environment (\texttt{axiom\_\allowbreak{}free}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:381}), concludes that the erased term evaluates to the erasure that \texttt{erase} computes of the source value, and that this \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value is first-order, a tree of constructor applications (\texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}evalue}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2027}); and \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}erases\_\allowbreak{}deterministic} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2079}), by which every erasure of a value of a first-order inductive type is the one \texttt{erase} computes.
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{EraseProof.erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} concludes what MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) concludes: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value is an erasure of the source value. Nothing states that it is a first-order value, or that the source value determines it.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} both first-order results are about terms whose type is an inductive type (\texttt{mkApps (tInd i u) args}), and \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}ind} holds only of a name declared as an inductive type. The fragment has none: lean4lean \texttt{master} has no inductive types (\texttt{Lean4Lean.VInductDecl.WF} and \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.addInduct} are \texttt{sorry} definitions, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Inductive.lean:5,7}; DV-6), so \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} admits no inductive declaration and no term in scope has an inductive result type. The hypothesis \texttt{axiom\_\allowbreak{}free} belongs to these results only (DV-21).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} stating the first-order corollary for the fragment: its hypothesis that the result type is a first-order inductive type never holds in scope, so the statement would be vacuous.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-20}{DV-20}}\label{reg:dv-20}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Simulation.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct}, the relation-level simulation: an evaluation (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}) of a well-typed closed source term to a value is matched by a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation (\texttt{EraseProof.LBEval} at \texttt{EraseProof.defaultFlags}) of any erasure of the term (\texttt{EraseProof.Erases}) whose dependencies are erased (\texttt{EraseProof.ErasesDeps}), to an erasure of the source value.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} Letouzey \S{}3.4: Theorem 12 (forward simulation, CIC\ensuremath{\Box} \ensuremath{\to} CIC: if \texttt{(\ensuremath{\Gamma}, t) \ensuremath{\blacktriangleleft} (\ensuremath{\Gamma}0, t0)} and \texttt{t \ensuremath{\to}rw u}, then \texttt{t0 \ensuremath{\to}rw+ u0} for some \texttt{u0} with \texttt{(\ensuremath{\Gamma}, u) \ensuremath{\blacktriangleleft} (\ensuremath{\Gamma}0, u0)}; Appendix A), Theorem 13 (backward simulation, CIC \ensuremath{\to} CIC\ensuremath{\Box}: if \texttt{(\ensuremath{\Gamma}, t) \ensuremath{\blacktriangleleft} (\ensuremath{\Gamma}0, t0)} and \texttt{t0 \ensuremath{\to}rw u0}, then \texttt{(\ensuremath{\Gamma}, u) \ensuremath{\blacktriangleleft} (\ensuremath{\Gamma}0, u0)} for some \texttt{u} with \texttt{t \ensuremath{\to}rw u} or \texttt{t \ensuremath{\to}*\ensuremath{\Box}w u}; Appendix B) and Theorem 15 (adequacy: every \texttt{\ensuremath{\to}rw\ensuremath{\Box}w} derivation from \texttt{\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}(t)}, for a well-typed closed \texttt{t} whose type is a logic-free data type, terminates on the CIC normal form of \texttt{t}; Appendix C). MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}; MetaCoq paper \S{}7.3, p. 8:64), which \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} follows: a big-step statement over PCUIC's \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}) and \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:119}) at \texttt{default\_\allowbreak{}wcbv\_\allowbreak{}flags}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} of Letouzey's three theorems, only Theorem 13 has a counterpart, and it is proved big-step at call-by-value, as MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} is: a whole source evaluation to a value, not a single weak step, is matched by a whole \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation, not by one step or by \ensuremath{\Box}-steps, and the invariant \ensuremath{\blacktriangleleft} (Definition 10) is the erasure relation \texttt{EraseProof.Erases} (MetaRocq's \texttt{erases}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}). Theorems 12 and 15 are omitted: nothing states that a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} step is matched by source steps (Theorem 12), or that the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} reductions of an erased closed term of a logic-free data type terminate on the term's normal form (Theorem 15).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Theorem 15 needs strong normalization of the source, for its termination half (Appendix C maps each step of the erased term to at least one source step by Theorem 12, and concludes by strong normalization), and data types (Definition 14), which are inductive types; lean4lean \texttt{master} has neither: it proves no normalization theorem, and \texttt{Lean4Lean.VInductDecl.WF} and \texttt{Lean4Lean.VEnv.addInduct} are \texttt{sorry} definitions (\texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Theory/\allowbreak{}Inductive.lean:5,7}; DV-6). Theorem 12 serves only Theorem 15's termination argument. MetaRocq, the machine-checked reference, replaces both by \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct}, which takes the source evaluation as a hypothesis and so needs no normalization; \texttt{EraseProof.erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} follows it.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} proving Theorem 12 on its own: without Theorem 15 it has no consumer on the path to the final theorem; a small-step Theorem 13 over weak reduction in any order, which says nothing about the value that \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s call-by-value evaluator reaches (DV-22); strong normalization as a hypothesis, a stand-in for a result lean4lean \texttt{master} lacks (spec \S{}2), and false in the fragment, which has diverging recursive unsafe constants (DV-22's \texttt{loop}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-21}{DV-21}}\label{reg:dv-21}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Env.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}: its rule \texttt{axiom} admits axioms, declarations without a value, in the program's environment; and \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}, which evaluates programs that use them.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} Letouzey \S{}3.4 (p. 10), "from now to the end of this paper we will only consider contexts with no assumptions", the hypothesis of Theorems 12, 13 and 15. MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}) has no such hypothesis: \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext \ensuremath{\Sigma}} admits constants without a body, and \texttt{axiom\_\allowbreak{}free} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:381}) is a hypothesis only of the first-order results, such as \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}firstorder} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2310}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} programs may depend on axioms: \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv} relates lists containing Lean \texttt{axiom} declarations to models in which they are constants without a defining equation. In evaluation an axiom has no \ensuremath{\delta} rule: an axiom whose declared type is evidently an arity or a proposition (\texttt{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom}, DV-11) is a value (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom}), and any other axiom is stuck (no rule of \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} evaluates it), as a constant without a body is in PCUIC's \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}). This follows MetaRocq and diverges from Letouzey.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the spec (\S{}2) puts in scope every input whose verification needs nothing beyond lean4lean \texttt{master}, and \texttt{master} models axioms (rule \texttt{axiom} of \texttt{Lean4Lean.TrEnv'}, \texttt{Lean4Lean/\allowbreak{}Verify/\allowbreak{}Environment/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean:134}). Letouzey needs the hypothesis for canonicity (a closed term of an inductive type reduces to a constructor), in the \ensuremath{\iota} cases of the proof of Theorem 12 (Appendix A, cases 1 and 2) and in Theorem 15; the fragment has no inductive types and no \ensuremath{\iota}-reduction (DV-6).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} excluding axioms from \texttt{EraseProof.ProgEnv}, as Letouzey does: it narrows the scope the spec fixes without a gap in \texttt{master} that forces it.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-22}{DV-22}}\label{reg:dv-22}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Source/\allowbreak{}Eval.lean}, \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval}: the source semantics is big-step, call-by-value evaluation.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} Letouzey \S{}3.4, Definition 9 (weak reductions: the \ensuremath{\beta}, \ensuremath{\iota}, \ensuremath{\delta}, \ensuremath{\zeta} and \ensuremath{\Box} steps, closed under application, on either side, and under case analysis, but not under \ensuremath{\lambda}, so in any order), for which Theorem 13 (backward simulation) is stated step by step. MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}) is stated for PCUIC's big-step weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}; MetaCoq paper \S{}5.6), which \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} follows.
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval} fixes one order, call-by-value: an application evaluates its function and its argument before the \ensuremath{\beta}-step (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.beta}), and a \texttt{let} its value before its body (\texttt{EraseProof.SrcEval.zeta}). Reductions in any other order, which Definition 9 admits, are not steps of the source semantics, which is big-step: it relates a term to its value, not to its one-step reducts.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the target is \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s call-by-value evaluation (\texttt{EraseProof.LBEval}, MetaRocq's \texttt{eval}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:119}, which peregrine implements), and a value reached in another order need not be reached by it: with the recursive \texttt{unsafe def loop : A \ensuremath{\to} A := fun x =\textgreater{} loop x} and \texttt{a : A}, \texttt{(fun \_\allowbreak{} =\textgreater{} a) (loop a)} reduces to \texttt{a} by one \ensuremath{\beta}-step, while \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation of its image evaluates \texttt{loop a} first and diverges. So the theorem, which is about the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluator, needs a source semantics that evaluates in the evaluator's order; MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} is stated in the same way.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} weak reduction in any order, as Definition 9, with a step-by-step simulation, as Theorem 13: it relates single steps and says nothing about the value the call-by-value evaluator reaches, and a value reached in another order need not be reached by it (above).
\end{itemize}
